title: What's Inside
logline: 2am at a truck stop, a long-haul driver reaches for {{product.name}}. The camera dives inside it to show, part by part, exactly what the product page says is in there, and nothing it does not.

ingested: ingredient lists are the classic dive: each named ingredient becomes a glowing model
applied: named actives in a cream, serum or balm float out of the formula
worn: works when the page names materials or layers (knit, foam, membrane, sole); weak if the page only says 'premium fabric'
handheld: an exploded view of the parts or specs the page names (battery, lens, chip, casing)
carried: named fabrics, frame, lining and compartments go translucent
home: Rosa uses it in the sleeper berth of her cab, so only pillows, blankets, lamps and small appliances fit; large furniture cannot be in the cab
consumable: the refill or pack is opened and its named contents explained

avoid: products whose page names fewer than 2 components
medicines, supplements or anything whose components would need medical or health claims
anything unsafe to use right before driving (sleep aids, sedatives)

product_extract.why: This template explains the product's own components. The standard product card has no field for them, so the runner extracts them here, from the product page only, before filling the template.

components.extract: Up to 4 components the product page itself names: ingredients from an ingredient list, actives, materials, fabrics, layers, parts or construction features from a materials or spec section, or 'made with' text. Keep the page's order or its emphasis. A component is only valid if its name appears on the page.

fields.name: the component's name exactly as written on the page
fields.page_quote: the exact page text that names it (copied, for the audit trail)
fields.amount: an amount, percentage, count or size ONLY if the page states it next to the component, else empty
fields.stated_function: what the component does, copied from the page ONLY if the page says it, else empty
fields.label: the post callout text: name, plus amount if stated, in capitals, 4 words or fewer
fields.visual: one sentence describing how the component is shown as a stylized 3D object in this world, following world_bible.materials_rule and the component look set asset (ingredients and actives as glossy ball-and-stick models, crystals or droplets; materials as a floating layer or panel of that material; parts as a floating exploded part). Describe shape and colour only, never text.

glow_colours.2: coral (a group may add lime, violet and cyan)

mapping.4: S04 = component 1, S05 = component 2, S06 = component 3, S07 = component 4.
mapping.3: S04 = component 1, S05 = component 2, S06 = component 3, S07 = all three together in a loose ring (use [[component.3.visual]] in S07 and add the other two in the same ring).
mapping.2: S04 and S05 = component 1 (S05 is a slower orbit around the same object), S06 and S07 = component 2. L3 names component 1, L4 gives its stated function or amount, L5 names component 2, L6 gives its stated function or amount (or the left_out payoff).
mapping.fewer: Fewer than 2 page-named components: the template does not fit. Stop at the fit check and suggest another template.

left_out.extract: OPTIONAL. One thing the page explicitly says the product is free of or made without ('no X', 'X-free', 'without X', 'free from X'). Only if the page states it word for word. Never infer it from an ingredient list.

fields.name: the thing left out, as the page words it
fields.visual: one sentence describing a large stylized novelty version of that thing in this world's materials_rule, no face, no letters

left_out.prop_prompt_template: Stylized 3D prop reference sheet on a plain mid-grey background, three views of one large [[left_out.visual]] in soft rounded Pixar-lite style, one small chip or dent for wear. No face, no letters or marks. Clean studio light, soft shadow. The object is isolated on a seamless plain mid-grey paper backdrop with nothing else in frame: no room, no set, no furniture, no products, no captions, no view labels, no text of any kind.
left_out.if_absent: Use the default text for [[S01.gag]] and [[S07.gag]], drop the bounce sound, and write L1 and L6 without it.

S01.gag.with_left_out: High in the upper right corner of the frame, far from the product with a wide gap of empty space between them, a large stylized [[left_out.visual]] is caught mid bounce, flying away from the product, with a short motion arc trailing to the upper right and a soft ripple on the glass where it hit. It never touches, crosses or enters the product.
S01.gag.default: A thin bright scan line sweeps down across the cutaway and faint glints of amber, coral, pearl white and mint show inside, one per component.

S07.gag.with_left_out: and on the other side of that clear wall, outside in the pale grey-blue void, a large stylized [[left_out.visual]] pressed against the glass, shut out, with no face
S07.gag.default: and behind it, softly out of focus, the earlier components glowing in a loose arc, all of them now lit

nothing_unstated: The narrator and the callouts may only say three things about a component: its name, an amount the page states, and a function the page states. Nothing else.

If stated_function is empty, the line names the component (and its stated amount, origin or count if any) and says nothing about what it does. Never add general knowledge about an ingredient, material or part, never 'which means', never science the page does not state.
Visuals may be stylized, but they must not imply a function the page does not state (no glowing arrows into a body, no before and after on skin, no health imagery).
No component is invented to fill a slot. With 2 or 3 components use the mapping; never pad to 4.
Benefit lines (L7) still come only from product.benefits.
product_extract.token_syntax: [[component.N.name]], [[component.N.label]], [[component.N.visual]], [[left_out.visual]], [[S01.gag]], [[S07.gag]] are filled from this block in Stage 3, right after the product card slots. No [[...]] token may remain in the fill.

lore: Rosa Delgado has driven for 22 years. Since her husband Manny died in 2021 she runs Delgado Freight alone, one truck out of El Paso, and the red cab is the same 2009 rig he bought used.
Tonight she is hauling a reefer trailer of avocados from Laredo to Kansas City, 940 miles, due on the dock at 7am. At Mile 212 she is nine hours into an eleven hour driving limit.
Mile 212 Stop is a 1968 fuel island with a six stool diner. The owner, Walt, has not turned the canopy lights off since the night of the 1996 blizzard, so drivers call it the lighthouse.

The inside of the product is imagined as a calm lab: one glowing platform for the product, and a far arc of four small pedestals, one per component glow colour (amber, coral, pearl white, mint), waiting to be lit as each component is shown.
Only what the product page names gets a pedestal. Anything the page does not state stays dark and is never shown or explained.
world_bible.materials_rule: Every object in the world is a soft stylized 3D model: rounded bevels on every edge, matte painted plastic and satin painted metal, simplified shapes with specific wear painted on as scuffs, chips, stickers-as-shapes and bug spatter; liquids glow softly from inside; nothing photoreal and no readable text anywhere. The product alone is photoreal and exact, in every shot where it appears whole.

world_bible.wear_and_time: 2:07am on a dry, cold desert night after a windy evening. The rig has 600 miles of bugs on the windshield, the diesel nozzle is still dripping from her fill-up, the diner is on its fourth pot of coffee and one roof clearance light has blown. Out of place: a tumbleweed jammed against the pump island. Inside the product everything is spotless until the components arrive.

a diesel engine idling with a low clatter

wind hissing across the empty lot
the product's own opening or use sound in the cab
soft bubble pops and glassy shimmers inside the void
a soft blip as each component arrives
air brakes sighing as the rig pulls away

beats.summary: The product in the void, cut away along one side, its inside glowing. The narrator names one surprising page-stated fact (with a left-out prop bouncing off if the page says it is free of something).
2am at a truck stop, Rosa uses the product in her cab; the camera dives into it.
The x-ray tour: up to four page-named components, one at a time, each lighting its pedestal; only what the page states is said.
Pull back out: the whole product rebuilds itself, label to camera. The brand line.
Rosa back on the dark highway, smiling, dawn on the horizon.
The product on a turntable in the void, one edge in x-ray, its components orbiting, tagline.

script.speaker: narrator
script.line_intent: Hook: one surprising true fact from the product page that makes the viewer ask 'wait, how?'. If left_out exists, pair how the product looks, feels or tastes with the thing it is free of.
script.delivery: fast, curious, friendly, a little conspiratorial
script.rules: the fact must be stated on the product page; left_out only if the page says it word for word

script.speaker: narrator
script.line_intent: Promise the explanation and set the scene.
script.fixed_line: So what's actually in there? Let's go inside.

script.speaker: narrator
script.line_intent: Component 1: 'First,' then its name, then its stated_function if the page gives one (else its stated amount, or nothing more).
script.delivery: clear, a beat on the component name
script.rules: name as written on the page; function only from stated_function, reworded no further than person and tense; nothing unstated (see product_extract.nothing_unstated)

script.speaker: narrator
script.line_intent: Component 2: 'Then' plus its name (a group may list its members as the page lists them), then its stated_function if the page gives one.
script.delivery: rapid list if it is a group, ticking each one, then slower on the function
script.rules: same as L3; spell hard names phonetically in the TTS script

script.speaker: narrator
script.line_intent: Component 3: 'Plus' and its name, with its stated amount or stated_function if the page gives one; if the page gives neither, the name alone.
script.rules: same as L3; with only 2 components follow product_extract.components.mapping

script.speaker: narrator
script.line_intent: Component 4, and pay off the hook: if left_out exists, name what the page uses instead and end on 'Not <left_out>.'; otherwise name component 4 with its stated function.
script.delivery: the reveal, a small grin, punch on the last two words
script.rules: same as L3; left_out wording from its page_quote only

script.speaker: narrator
script.line_intent: Product line: say {{product.name}} and its one point of difference from product.benefits.
script.delivery: warm and certain, slower than the rest
script.rules: benefit only from product.benefits, reworded no further than person and tense; brand spelled with product.phonetic in the TTS script

script.speaker: narrator
script.line_intent: Tagline: product.tagline if the page has one, otherwise a 3 to 5 word line about knowing exactly what is inside.
